reference: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve Diet & Prey Profile Chart

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Target apex predator under biometric individual Re-ID monitoring.
classes.morphology_notes: Distinct vertical black stripes on tawny/orange coat, white ventral areas, sexual dimorphism in skull/body size.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: High contrast stripe patterns clearly visible in night IR and color daylight.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Accounts for 35-50% of tiger biomass consumption in Central Indian dry-deciduous forests.
classes.morphology_notes: Large robust deer, uniform dark brown/slate coat, shaggy mane around neck in males, large rugose 3-tined antlers in stags.
confusion_risk_pairs: chital (large solitary stags in blurry IR)
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Tall shoulder height (>120cm), prominent rounded ears, highly nocturnal activity.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Major staple prey (15-25% of kills) and frequent village agricultural crop-raider.
classes.morphology_notes: Stocky barrel-shaped body, dark bristly coat, erect mane along spine, tapering snout, visible canine tusks in adult males.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Low ground clearance, head held low to ground, fast erratic movement causing motion blur.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Most abundant prey species by numerical frequency in Central Indian grasslands and meadows.
classes.morphology_notes: Golden-rufous coat with permanent white spots, white throat bib, slender legs, lyriform 3-tined antlers in stags.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: White spots remain discernible in night IR camera traps; high gregarious herding behavior.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Frequent conflict prey in buffer zones and corridor fringes; drives human-wildlife compensation claims.
classes.morphology_notes: Pronounced thoracic hump, large drooping dewlap, variable white/brown/piebald coloration, domestic collar or bell occasionally visible.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Prominent thoracic hump and neck dewlap distinguish from wild ungulates.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Solitary dense undergrowth prey; valuable forest interior indicator.
classes.morphology_notes: Small reddish-brown deer, hunched back posture, short antlers mounted on long skin-covered pedicels, dark facial ribs.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Very short shoulder height (40-65cm), distinct arched spine posture.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Largest extant bovine prey species; represents high-calorie kills by prime adult male tigers.
classes.morphology_notes: Massive muscular build, prominent dorsal ridge along back, dark brown to jet black coat, white/pale 'stockings' on all four lower legs, curved horns with pale bases.
confusion_risk_pairs: buffalo (domestic water buffalo in dim night frames)
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Extreme height/mass, prominent muscular dorsal ridge and high contrast white stocking legs.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Open scrub and buffer zone prey; highest biomass ungulate in degraded peripheral habitats.
classes.morphology_notes: Sloping back (forelegs longer than hindlegs), adult males slate-grey/blue with short horns and throat tuft; females tawny brown hornless.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Strong sloping backline from high shoulders down to rump; distinctive neck mane and tuft.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Sympatric carnivore; subject of territorial agonistic encounters and opportunistic predation.
classes.morphology_notes: Shaggy long black coat, pale whitish Y/V-shaped chest mark, cream-colored muzzle, long pale ivory digging claws.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Ambling shaggy gait, distinct pale snout reflecting IR illumination.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: High-risk village fringe livestock; primary victim of sub-adult dispersing tiger attacks near settlements.
classes.morphology_notes: Small stature, upturned tail, variable coloration, backward arching horns or polled, domestic collars.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Short body length (<90cm), upturned tail, active daytime/twilight village proximity.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Minor supplementary prey for tiger cubs and sub-adults; common nocturnal camera-trap capture.
classes.morphology_notes: Long upright ears with dark tips, black patch on nape of neck, rufous-brown grizzled fur, long hind limbs.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Very small bounding box (<5% of frame), prominent upright ears, distinct bounding gait.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: High-value buffer village livestock; kills generate substantial conflict tension with local pastoralists.
classes.morphology_notes: Sparse dark slate/black coat, long crescent-shaped horns sweeping backward, broad flat forehead, absence of white stockings.
confusion_risk_pairs: gaur (adult cows and sub-adults in night IR)
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Lack of dorsal crest and lack of white leg stockings distinguish reliably from wild Gaur.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Ground-dwelling avian prey; endemic to peninsular India, common diurnal undergrowth capture.
classes.morphology_notes: Gallinaceous body, male has finely barred grey plumage with yellow spotted neck hackles and curved tail; female mottled brown.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Ground foraging profile, bipedal avian posture, active primarily during dawn/dusk daylight.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Abundant terrestrial avian prey; key vocal alarm caller warning ungulates of tiger presence.
classes.morphology_notes: Male has iridescent blue neck, fan-shaped head crest, and long ornamental train; female is mottled brown with white belly and crest.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Long tail/train trail in males, erect fan-crest on head, large avian bounding box.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Nocturnal arboreal prey; occasional opportunistic kill when gliding between forest strata.
classes.morphology_notes: Large arboreal rodent, reddish-chestnut/grizzled dorsal fur, gliding membrane (patagium) between limbs, bushy cylindrical tail longer than body.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Exclusively nocturnal; captured climbing vertical tree trunks or gliding across canopy camera angles.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Key symbiotic vigilance partner with chital; high-pitched alarm calls signal stalking tigers.
classes.morphology_notes: Slender greyish-buff body, jet black hairless face with pale brow band, long limbs, long tail looping over back.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Distinct quadrupedal posture with long arched tail held higher than spine; bipedal sitting posture.

classes.tadoba_diet_relevance: Small opportunistic carnivore; common camera-trap capture along forest firebreaks and trail fringes.
classes.morphology_notes: Tawny-grey grizzled coat, long bushy tapering tail, short legs, pointed muzzle, low elongated profile.
classes.ir_camera_trap_profile: Very low ground silhouette (<20cm height), elongated body moving along trail edges.
